text.p: September T-bond futures are on shaky ground and must hurdle 114-30 if they are to regain a more positive tone, analysts said on Thursday.
But as long as they remain under the double top at 116-31, the market is vulnerable to a further correction, they added.
Raynard Cheng, technical analyst at First Chicago in London, was fairly optimistic on the contract, saying it would likely overcome resistance at 114-30.
He said that level was the 24 percent retracement of the move down from 116-31 on August 1 to 114-10 on August 6. It also almost coincides with Wednesday's high of 114-29, he added.
Above there, further resistance comes in at 115-10, the 38 percent retracement of the same move, followed by 115-20, said Cheng.
"I think we've based, seen the low," he said.
By 0942 GMT, September T-bonds were up 1/32 at 114-25.

Anil Patel, technical analyst at Nomura International in London, was much more negative, saying a bearish flag was developing on the charts which, if sucessful, would take T-bonds back to the low 113s.
"There is a double top in place at 116-31 which is a crucial level," he said. "With this big down movement we have a pole and a potential bear flag coming up."
He said there had been congestion from 115-00 to 114-10 over the past few days and to dispell the potential pattern a move back up to 115-31 would be needed.
To the downside Patel saw initial support around 114-04, the July 21 open.
"A break-out there would take us to 113-27 and from there the key level is 113-07," he said.
The daily chart shows the market hit a low of 113-27 on July 21 and a low of 113-07 on July 15.
Cheng said intraday trendline support came in at 114-16, followed by 114-10, the lows on August 5 and 6.
By 0942 GMT, December Eurodollars were up 0.010 at 94.095.
